label: first copy-phase step(s) of long (L=9) sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely on the first copy step after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, input = the echoed first original token; 77% of mass) and the second (recall_idx 2; 22%), and almost only for long sequences (L=9: 83% of mass, L=8: 16%, never L<=6). Equivalently, it fires when 6-7 outputs remain. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, or on the first occurrence of a token. Magnitude depends strongly on the identity of the echoed token: the strongest activations (top examples ~0.03) are at recall_idx 1 with first token j or k (precision 0.93 for L=9, j/k at recall_idx 1), then z, p, c, u. Tokens like o, a, g, f, q, x usually do not fire, which explains the low precision. The predicate (recall_idx==1)&(L==9) gets dev F1 0.48 with mass recall 0.64. Adding recall_idx 2 raises mass recall to 0.82 but lowers precision to 0.29. Small tail activations at the last copy steps (recall_idx 6-8) are not covered.
